issues.description: Method name mismatch for computing a meal's total price: the problem statement and UML require a method named calculateTotalPrice(Meal): int (and state it should be static), but the solution implements a static method named computeMealCost(Meal) and the template/solution commented examples reference both names inconsistently. This naming inconsistency can confuse students about which method to implement and call.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent method name across problem statement, template examples, and implementation. Prefer renaming the solution's computeMealCost(Meal) to calculateTotalPrice(Meal) (keeping it static and returning int) and update any example calls in Main or comments to call calculateTotalPrice. Alternatively, update the problem statement/UML to use computeMealCost if that name is preferred.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies a method named calculateTotalPrice(Meal) as the operation to compute a meal's total price, but the implementation in the repositories uses the identifier computeMealCost for the same concept. Template/Main (template repository) calls computeMealCost, and SealSaloon in the solution repository implements computeMealCost, while the problem UML and task text refer to calculateTotalPrice. This inconsistent naming of the same conceptual operation (compute/calculate total price of a Meal) creates mapping confusion for students and can cause missing/incorrect method calls across files.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent name for the operation across all artifacts. Rename computeMealCost to calculateTotalPrice in SealSaloon (and update its signature/callers), and update any Main/template calls to calculateTotalPrice. Alternatively, update the problem statement/UML to reference computeMealCost if that name is preferred — but ensure all repositories and examples use the same identifier.
